text:
rachel: quick design sync - i ran into ambiguity when normalizing cost across model variants (fp16 vs int8 vs 4-bit) and different GPU classes. want to align on unit semantics before i land the policy changes.

omar: good call. core question: is "cost" a pure $$ estimate, a latency proxy, or a composite score we use for ranking? we need consistent semantics.

jen: in my view cost should be a unitless score exposed by the runtime that downstream policy can map to dollars or latency as needed. keeps policy agnostic to billing changes.

vishal: counterpoint: ops needs transparent dollar estimates for tenant chargebacks and fair preemption. mixing units hides incentives.

rachel: proposal: split values: runtime publishes three primitives per route-model-region: perf_ms (p95), token_cost_usd, norm_score. policy engine ranks on norm_score but console shows token_cost_usd.

omar: how do we compute norm_score? need to account for seq-len sensitivity and KV cache hits. also normalization across GPU capability (A100 vs H100) and quantization quality delta.

jen: suggested formula prototype: norm_score = w_latency * f(latency) + w_cost * g(cost) + w_quality * h(quality_penalty) where each term normalized to [0,1]. quality_penalty is 0 for baseline model, increases based on eval regressions vs prod prompt-set.

vishal: we must avoid double-counting: cost_usd already correlates with latency. maybe decorrelate by using residuals: latency_resid = latency - E[latency | cost_usd, seq_len]. That removes the predictable part.

rachel: oo interesting. compute a simple regression per-model-family to get expected latency given cost and seq_len, then use residual as latency signal. keeps norm_score focused on unexpected slowness.

omar: implementation: metrics pipeline computes per-model-family baseline regression and writes model_baseline entries to the route cache. policy runtime reads baseline and raw metrics and computes norm_score. keep computation lightweight.

jen: pseudocode (rough):
```
baseline = read_baseline(model_family)
expected_latency = baseline.a * cost_usd + baseline.b * seq_len + baseline.c
lat_resid = max(0, observed_latency - expected_latency)
quality = clamp( eval_regression_score, 0, 1 )
norm = normalize( w_l*lat_resid + w_c*cost_usd + w_q*quality )
```

vishal: normalization and weights must be tenant-aware. enterprise tenants may prefer quality heavy; small startups prefer cost. add per-tenant weight overrides and a global auto-mode.

rachel: policy surface change: add optional fields to route selector: prefer_weights: {latency, cost, quality} and model_family_preference list. must be backward compatible: default picks balanced weights.

omar: what about model-variant hygiene? runtime may have several quantized variants with different quality deltas. policy must only compare compatible variants or apply explicit quality penalty when using cheaper variant.

jen: introduce variant_compatibility metadata with fields: quality_factor, cost_multiplier, compatible_with: [families]. policy ranking should only cross-compare variants after applying cost_multiplier and quality_factor. also add a contract: mixture of variants is allowed only if tenant policy opts in.

vishal: migration: older policies don't include variant_compatibility. default behavior: treat unknown variant as quality_factor=0 (no penalty) but tag decisions as "compatibility_unknown" for audit. better to be conservative: maybe default quality_factor=0.1 to avoid accidental low-quality routes.

rachel: agree on conservative default. also need explainability: each decision should include breakdown: model_variant, perf_ms, token_cost_usd, quality_penalty, norm_score, baseline_version. expose in trace.

omar: runtime perf note: computing regression and residual per model-family can be done in metrics consumer; policy runtime only applies small arithmetic ops. avoids heavy per-request work. also support precompute buckets for hot routes.

jen: tests: unit on normalization math, end-to-end sim with mixed variants and seq_len distributions, and canary traffic where cheaper variant is flagged to ensure quality alerts trigger.

vishal: ops/UI: need a "variant impact" view showing expected quality delta and cost savings per-tenant if they opt into cheap variants. plus an emergency "rollback variants" knob.

infra-bot: rollout plan created: rollout/variant-score-normalization-2026-03-21 -> 4% dedicated eu-west1

rachel: final notes: i'll draft RFC with the formula, migration rules, variant metadata schema, and console mocks. tagging @eng-runtime @eng-platform for review.

omar: :thumbsup: i'll review the regression math.

jen: i'll do the simulation scenarios.

vishal: i'll design the ops surface and emergency procedures.
